original_question: What is the least possible degree of a function f : {-1,1}^n -> [-1,-2/3] union [2/3,1] such that f(x) lies in [2/3,1] whenever sum_i x_i >= n/2 and lies in [-1,-2/3] whenever sum_i x_i <= -n/2?
target_in_paper: Section 3 (Boolean functions), the standalone open problem titled "Approximate Degree for Approximate Majority" on page 13.
correct_elements: Your draft is already extremely close to the paper’s official formulation: it matches the domain {-1,1}^n, the codomain [-1,-2/3]∪[2/3,1], the upper-threshold condition sum_i x_i >= n/2, the lower-threshold condition sum_i x_i <= -n/2, and the fact that one asks for the least possible degree. Because you stated the full codomain restriction, your draft also already implies the paper’s remark that f must avoid (-2/3,2/3) even on the middle layers.
missing_details: Specify what "degree" means: the total degree of the unique multilinear polynomial over R that agrees with f on {-1,1}^n (equivalently, the Fourier degree / real polynomial degree on the hypercube).
Make the quantifier explicit: for each fixed positive integer n, minimize over all such functions f, i.e. determine this minimum as a function of n.
State explicitly that f is real-valued; the output intervals live in R, so the ambient field/range is R.

If making the question fully stand-alone, note explicitly that no output in (-2/3,2/3) is allowed on any input, including those with -n/2 < sum_i x_i < n/2; the paper flags this in the remark even though it is implicit in the codomain.
refined_question: For each positive integer n, determine the minimum possible degree deg(f) of a real-valued function f:{-1,1}^n -> [-1,-2/3]∪[2/3,1], where deg(f) denotes the total degree of the unique multilinear polynomial over R agreeing with f on {-1,1}^n, subject to the conditions that f(x) ∈ [2/3,1] whenever sum_{i=1}^n x_i >= n/2 and f(x) ∈ [-1,-2/3] whenever sum_{i=1}^n x_i <= -n/2.
justification: The draft is targeting the exact open problem in the paper, not a neighboring conjecture. The official formulation appears verbatim under the heading "Approximate Degree for Approximate Majority" in Section 3 on page 13. The only substantive sharpening needed to make the question fully stand-alone is to define "degree" in the paper’s standard sense, namely multilinear real-polynomial/Fourier degree, which is set up in Section 2 under "Functions given by polynomials." The nearby remark on page 13 confirms that the codomain restriction applies on the middle layers as well. The paper does not provide a numbered equivalent reformulation here, so no alternate formulation should be added.
